A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CogCoM and Chain of Manipulations. All 17 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison. Methods, equations, experiments, and figures can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original CogCoM benchmark results, reasoning-training curves, data-generation statistics, and qualitative outputs in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds MM-Vet scores and measurements of inference time and output length in Section 5.

M1.justification: v2 adds Line(pts) → img to the five predefined manipulations and demonstrates drawing auxiliary lines and processing the resulting images. The 17B architecture, KV-memory attention, training objective, and automatic annotation/DFS pipeline remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 expands coverage with MM-Vet evaluation of integrated multimodal capabilities and graphical mathematics, including a geometry demonstration and 6K MathVista/ChartQA annotations in Section 3.2. The exact incorporation of these annotations into training is not consistently documented, and no quantitative math-benchmark evaluation appears. The original benchmark coverage remains; AutoCoM-test is renamed CoM-test.

E2.justification: Table 3 removes MiniGPT4, which had a reported POPE score of 70.4 in v1. Other removed rows previously contained dashes and therefore do not establish removed evaluated comparisons. Comparator membership in the VQA and grounding tables is unchanged; MM-Vet uses methods already compared elsewhere.

E3.justification: v2 adds latency/token measurements over 218 MM-Vet questions grouped into eight time bins. CoM-test is described as using TextVQA's test rather than validation split, and the manipulation-distribution caption changes five-shot to four-shot prompting. Table 5 changes alignment data from 570K to 576K, although Section 4.2 retains 570K. These reported revisions do not establish rerunning retained experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds comparative inference-cost analysis in Figure 6 and an analysis grouping actions into six manipulations in Figure 3. Figure 1 replaces several qualitative cases with chart-line, hallucination, and geometry examples. The original CoM-only training analysis and several existing cases remain; there is no substantial new ablation or robustness suite.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, uncertainty bars, or significance tests. The new latency-bin averages are point summaries, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports MM-Vet scores of 46.1 for CogCoM and 45.5 for CogVLM, latency/token profiles, and a generation-success rate of 0.3555. MiniGPT4's POPE result is removed. Tables 1–2, shared POPE scores, and the reasoning-training curve retain their results; the additions do not demonstrate improved performance between versions.

T1.justification: The formal allowable-manipulation set gains Line(pts) → img in Section 2. Otherwise, the chain structure, KV-memory attention equations, and composite Levenshtein/BLEU metric remain equivalent, including the metric retained in Appendix C.2. No new theorem, proof, or formal complexity derivation is provided.

C1.justification: v2 adds the 6K graphical-math resource as a headline contribution and expands claimed benchmark coverage from eight benchmarks in three categories to nine in four. The central interpretable-reasoning claim remains. Its new 1.09-point grounding-improvement claim is not explained by Table 2, whose largest gain over CogVLM is 0.99.

C2.justification: v2 interprets its runtime results as informative reasoning without infeasible time overhead and MM-Vet results as preservation of general capabilities. It removes v1 Section 3.1.2's specific warning that the reasoning metric over-penalizes approximate results such as similar boxes. Most other limitations are preserved in Appendices B and C.5.

D1.justification: v2 discloses 3,840, 256, and 160 A100-days for the training phases and identifies ten human annotators. It removes documentation of v1's area-ratio crop/zoom insertion rule, including the r ≥ 36 example. Stated resource access changes from linked public code/data availability to a future code/weights/data release promise without a link; actual online availability is not established.

R1.justification: v2 adds AlphaGeometry, MathVista, ChartQA, MM-Vet, and KVQuant citations supporting the mathematical extension, evaluation, and efficiency discussion. MiniGPT4 and LLaMA-Adapter v2 references disappear with table pruning. The two related-work subsections remain substantively similar, so research positioning changes locally.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and introduction and reorganizes the former Methodology section into separate Terminology, Data Collection, and Model Training sections. Limitations, impacts, and qualitative-analysis discussion move into appendices. This substantially changes the narrative structure beyond renaming and renumbering.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. v2 introduces an opening example gallery, redraws the motivating schematic, and separates/redraws the combined data-generation and architecture diagram. It adds action-mapping and latency panels and restructures Table 3 with LLM and MM-Vet columns, while reusing several existing examples and plots.

improvement.justification: MM-Vet evaluation, runtime measurements, and hardware disclosure improve evidence about breadth and practical cost. However, v2 loses useful crop/zoom details, the metric caveat, and the resource link, while introducing conflicting training totals and a grounding-gain claim inconsistent with Table 2. The mathematical extension's training role and empirical benefit also remain unclear. These competing gains and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
